## `childrenOf` method

The `childrenOf` method resolves the children of a node, with special handling for fragment spreads. If the node is not a `FragmentSpread`, it returns `node.getChildren()`. Otherwise, it casts to `FragmentSpread` and returns a singleton list containing the fragment definition looked up by name via `fragmentsByName.get(fragmentSpread.getName())`.

## `visitImpl` and root variables (`rootVars`)

The core traversal logic lives in `visitImpl`, which sets up the root variables map. In the current master version, a `Map<Class<?>, Object> rootVars` is created as a `LinkedHashMap`, and the `QueryTraversalContext.class` key is populated with `new QueryTraversalContext(rootParentType, null, null, GraphQLContext.getDefault())`.

It then configures pre-order and post-order callbacks. If `preOrder` is null, both the `preOrderCallback` and `postOrderCallback` are set to the supplied `visitFieldCallback`. Otherwise, a no-op `QueryVisitorStub` is created, and the `preOrderCallback` is set to `visitFieldCallback` if `preOrder` is true (else the no-op), while the `postOrderCallback` is set to `visitFieldCallback` if `preOrder` is false.

Finally, it performs the traversal: a `NodeTraverser` is constructed with `rootVars` and the `this::childrenOf` method reference, a `NodeVisitorWithTypeTracking` is created with the pre/post-order callbacks, variables, schema, and `fragmentsByName`, and then `nodeTraverser.depthFirst(nodeVisitorWithTypeTracking, roots)` is returned.

## `transform` method

The `transform` method uses a tree transformer rather than a plain traverser. It creates a no-op `QueryVisitorStub`, builds a `NodeVisitorWithTypeTracking` using the supplied `queryVisitor`, the no-op, variables, schema, and `fragmentsByName`, then sets up `rootVars` as a `LinkedHashMap` with a `QueryTraversalContext`. It defines a `TraverserVisitor<Node>` whose `enter` method sets the `LeaveOrEnter.ENTER` var and dispatches via `context.thisNode().accept(context, nodeVisitor)`, while its `leave` method simply returns `TraversalControl.CONTINUE` because transformations are applied pre-order only. It then returns `new TreeTransformer<>(AST_NODE_ADAPTER).transform(root, nodeTraverserVisitor, rootVars)`.

## Constructor / field setup

The traverser is initialized from the document operation: `NodeUtil.getOperation(document, operation)` produces a result whose `fragmentsByName` is stored, `roots` is set to a singleton list of the operation definition, and `rootParentType` is derived via `getRootTypeFromOperation`. There are also assertions ensuring `rootParentType` and `fragmentsByName` are non-null, tied to building with an arbitrary `root(Node)` and `rootParentType(GraphQLCompositeType)`.

## Notes on behavior and context

Some helpful context about what this traversal does and its history:

- `QueryTraversal`, built on top of `NodeVisitor`, allows traversing a query while tracking schema information — meaning you get the actual type information for every field visited — and `QueryTraversalContext` tracks the current type information.

- The built-in `skip`/`include` directives are automatically evaluated so ignored parts of the Document are not visited, but this is not a full evaluation of the query — every fragment will be visited/followed regardless of the type condition, and field merging is not considered (e.g., `{ user{firstName} user{firstName}}` results in four `visitField` calls).

- The `QueryTraversal` class was made a public API through a PR that makes it public (it was internal before) and improves it by allowing an arbitrary `Node` as the root (not only the `DocumentDefinition`) and adds the `SelectionSetContainer` to the environment.

One important caveat regarding versions: there is a difference in the `QueryTraversalContext` constructor arguments between versions. If you're implementing against a specific version, check the constructor signature carefully.
